'''Yael Tauman Kalai''' ({{Langx|he|יעל טאומן קלעי}}) is a [[cryptography|cryptographer]] and [[theoretical computer science|theoretical computer scientist]] and the Ellen Swallow Richards Professor at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] in the [[MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory|Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory]].{{r|mit}} Previously, she worked as a Senior Principal Researcher at [[Microsoft Research New England]]{{r|mrne|simons}}.

==Education and career==
Kalai graduated from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 1997. She earned a master's degree in 2001 at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], working with [[Adi Shamir]], and then completed a PhD advised by [[Shafi Goldwasser]] at MIT in 2006. After postdoctoral study at Microsoft Research and the Weizmann Institute, she became a faculty member at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]]. She took a permanent position at Microsoft Research in 2008{{r|mrne|simons}} and became a professor at MIT in 2024.<ref name="h043">{{cite web | last=Goodale | first=Zach | title=School of Engineering welcomes new faculty | website=MIT News | date=2024-05-23 | url=https://news.mit.edu/2024/school-engineering-welcomes-new-faculty-0523 }}</ref> She serves on the Scientific Advisory Board of the [[Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing]].{{r|simons-advisory}}

==Contributions==
Kalai is known for co-inventing [[ring signature]]s, which have become a key component of numerous systems such as [[Cryptonote]] and [[Monero (cryptocurrency)]].{{r|ring|iacr}} Subsequently, together with her advisor [[Shafi Goldwasser]], she demonstrated an insecurity in the widely used [[Fiat–Shamir heuristic]].{{r|fiatshamir|iacr}}  Her work on [[Verifiable computing|delegating computation]] has applications to cloud computing.{{r|cloud}}

==Recognition==
Kalai was elected a Fellow of the [[International Association for Cryptologic Research]] in 2022 for foundational contributions in delegated computation and leakage-resilient cryptography, and service to the cryptographic community.{{r|iacr}}

Kalai was an invited speaker on mathematical aspects of computer science at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].{{r|icm}}

Her master's thesis introducing [[ring signature]]s won an outstanding master's thesis award{{r|simons}} and her MIT PhD dissertation was awarded the George M. Sprowls Award for Outstanding PhD Thesis in Computer Science.{{r|simons}}{{r|sprowls}}

She was co-chair of the [[Theory of Cryptography Conference]] in 2017.{{r|tcc}}

She was awarded the 2022 [[ACM Prize in Computing]] "for breakthroughs in verifiable delegation of computation and fundamental contributions to cryptography".{{r|acm}}
	 	
==Personal==

Kalai is the daughter of game theorist [[Yair Tauman]].{{r|quanta}} Her husband, [[Adam Tauman Kalai]], works at OpenAI.{{r|bliss|adam}}
